whatThePageStates: The page explains the service-linked roles (SLRs) that AWS Security Incident Response uses. It opens with a one-line assertion, "Supports service-linked roles: Yes", then documents two named roles (AWSServiceRoleForSecurityIncidentResponse and AWSServiceRoleForSecurityIncidentResponse_Triage), giving for each the trusted service principal, the attached AWS managed policy, a prose list of what the role is permitted to do, and how the role is created and deleted. It then has a section "Supported regions for AWS Security Incident Response service-linked roles" that says SLRs are supported in all regions where the service is available and lists 25 named regions as bullets. A final section explains that expected InvalidInputException entries for CreateServiceLinkedRole appear in CloudTrail, and a "See also" block advertises optional AI-coding-assistant skills. The only enumerable coverage claim on the page is the region list; everything else is narrative or a single-service boolean.

features.featureName: Supported regions for AWS Security Incident Response service-linked roles
features.statuses: 25 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 25+0+0=25. Every bullet under the "Supported regions" heading is an unqualified positive: the region is listed, therefore SLRs are supported there. There is no No column, no strikethrough, no exclusion note, and no 'except' sentence, so not-supported is never STATED anywhere on this page — it is only implied by absence from the list, which is not a coverage claim. Region bullets counted in listed order: US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), US East (Virginia), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Milan), Europe (Paris), Europe (Spain), Europe (Stockholm), Europe (Zurich), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Middle East (Bahrain), Middle East (UAE), South America (Sao Paulo), Africa (Cape Town) = 25.
features.scope: None. The list is stated once for "AWS Security Incident Response service-linked roles" collectively; it is NOT broken down per role, so it cannot be split into a per-role dimension. The page names two SLRs but gives no per-role region table, no per-partition breakdown (no GovCloud or China entries at all), and no per-plan or per-account-type qualifier. The one soft qualifier is the sentence 'supports using service-linked roles in all of the regions where the service is available', which ties the list to service availability rather than adding a second dimension.
features.reasoning: The bullets are AWS Region display names drawn from the universe of AWS Regions, which exists independently of Security Incident Response, so the axis is the external `region` axis. The unit of claim is one region per bullet: each bullet asserts that SLRs for this service can be used in that region. Rows do not collapse — each of the 25 bullets names a different region, so the row count and the distinct-target count are both 25 and the optional collapse fields are omitted.

shouldNotExtract: The permission prose is not coverage. The 7 bullets under AWSServiceRoleForSecurityIncidentResponse (AWS Organizations, CreateCase, ListCases, UpdateCase, CreateCaseComment, ListComments, TagResource) and the 5 bullets under AWSServiceRoleForSecurityIncidentResponse_Triage (Events, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub CSPM, AWS Identity and Access Management, AWS Security Incident Response) describe what a role may do; they are a mixed bag of service names and API operation names with no Yes/No status, and they are NOT a supported-service, supported-resource-type or supported-api-operation matrix. Also not coverage: the 4-item Topics navigation list at the top; the two trusted-principal bullets (security-ir.amazonaws.com, triage.security-ir.amazonaws.com); the managed-policy links; the 'Managing the role' console-versus-API/CLI instructions; the entire 'Expected CreateServiceLinkedRole events in AWS CloudTrail' section, which is troubleshooting narrative about an InvalidInputException and contains no enumeration; and the 'See also' AI-coding-assistant / Agent Toolkit boilerplate with its aws agent-toolkit search-skills command.
coverageDimensions: REGION: this is the only dimension the page actually measures — 25 named regions, all positive, no negatives stated. SERVICE: the page gives nothing usable. It is about exactly one service (AWS Security Incident Response), and the 'Supports service-linked roles: Yes' line is a single boolean about that one service, not an enumeration; the other AWS service names that appear (Organizations, GuardDuty, Security Hub CSPM, IAM, EventBridge) appear inside permission descriptions and carry no support status, so any per-service coverage figure taken from this page is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE: the page gives nothing at all — no resource types are enumerated and no resource-type support status is stated anywhere; a resource-type count from this page would be invented.
trap: The single most likely misparse is harvesting the role-permission bullets as a supported-service or supported-resource-type list: 'The service uses the role to perform actions on the following resources:' reads like a resource enumeration, so a careless parser yields 7 and/or 5 items (or 12 combined) as covered services or resource types, when they are permission descriptions with no support status and mix service names with API operation names. Runners-up: (1) treating 'Supports service-linked roles: Yes' as a one-value coverage matrix, or multiplying it into a per-service claim; (2) counting the 4 Topics nav links as coverage rows; (3) inferring No for every unlisted AWS Region — absence from the region list is not a stated negative, and the page never enumerates a negative; (4) splitting the 25 regions across the two named roles to produce 50; (5) treating the two SLR names as an axis, when the page's only enumerated axis is region; (6) scraping the 'See also' Agent Toolkit block as feature content.
